# Totem

> Totem is a local-first Chrome extension that turns X / Twitter bookmarks into a searchable read-later queue on every new tab, with a clean reader, reading progress, highlights, notes, and export/import.

Totem is built for people who save posts on X but want to read, search, annotate, and own that library outside the X feed. It runs in the browser, reads from the user's existing X session, and stores bookmarks, notes, highlights, and reading progress locally. There is no Totem account, backend sync service, or product telemetry.

Use the official product and schema pages first. Use blog articles for topic-specific explanations about X bookmarks, export behavior, bookmark privacy, and related read-later tools.

## Product

- [Totem homepage](https://usetotem.xyz/): Product overview, core positioning, install link, and feature summary.
- [Live demo](https://usetotem.xyz/demo/): Interactive demo of the Totem new-tab bookmark reader experience.
- [How Totem works](https://usetotem.xyz/how-it-works/): Interactive map of the extension data flow, storage keys, and implementation files.
- [Privacy policy](https://usetotem.xyz/privacy): Plain-English policy covering X access, local browser storage, permissions, and what stays on the device.

## Documentation

- [Totem Export Format v1](https://usetotem.xyz/export-format/v1): Version-pinned schema for Totem export ZIPs, including manifest, JSONL stores, CSV fields, Markdown files, checksums, and re-import behavior.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nnnkit/totem): Source code for the Chrome extension, website, export logic, reader UI, service worker, and local storage model.
- [Chrome Web Store listing](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/acpkgdfhoaalmnhjifhneghcgfnjkglo): Install page for the production Chrome extension.

## X Bookmark Guides

- [How to Export Your X / Twitter Bookmarks](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/how-to-export-twitter-bookmarks): Practical comparison of export methods and when CSV, Markdown, or a restorable backup is needed.
- [What Actually Gets Exported When You Export Twitter Bookmarks?](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/what-gets-exported-twitter-bookmarks): Explains URLs, CSV rows, Markdown files, local JSONL data, highlights, reading progress, and importability.
- [How to Search Your Twitter Bookmarks Before You Export Them](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/search-twitter-bookmarks-before-export): Search workflows for X bookmarks by person, phrase, domain, media, thread, and age before exporting.
- [Twitter Saver: What Saving Actually Does](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/twitter-saver-what-saving-actually-does): Explains the difference between saving, reading, exporting, and backing up Twitter/X posts.
- [Where Are My Bookmarks on X?](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/where-are-my-bookmarks-on-x): Shows how to find X bookmarks and why saved posts are easy to forget.
- [Why Your Twitter/X Bookmarks Disappear](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/twitter-x-bookmark-limit-explained): Explanation of X's visible bookmark window and the practical bookmark limit users encounter.
- [Are X / Twitter Bookmarks Private?](https://usetotem.xyz/blog/are-x-twitter-bookmarks-private): Explains what is private, what bookmark counts reveal, and what X changed in 2023.
